subject: Request: split RTO/RPO commitments for multi-region failover
messages:
From: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@nectarfin.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Nectar Security <security@nectarfin.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: SLA question — split RTO/RPO commitments for multi-region failover

Hi Karthik,

Quick question on the SLA language for multi-region failover in the draft we received last week. Our operations team had a runbook review and wants to ensure the EU region switchover has a faster RTO than the warm-standby commitment you've listed for global customers. Practically, we need a 30-minute RTO for EU failover events that impact retail traffic and can accept a longer RPO (up to 1 hour) for non-critical analytic pipelines.

I know this is a deviation from Redwood's standard uniform RTO/RPO, so we'd like to request a carveout/addendum for Nectar that specifies:
- EU retail traffic: RTO = 00:30, RPO = 00:10
- Non-critical analytics (EU): RTO = 02:00, RPO = 01:00

Can Redwood provide a proposal that maps these priorities against your model routing/standby tiers and notes any operational or cost implications? We can share runbook excerpts and a short network diagram.

Thanks — we have a contract kickoff with procurement next Wednesday, so timing is tight.

Carlos
VP, Platform Engineering
Nectar Financial

Attachment: runbook_excerpt.docx (referenced)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@nectarfin.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA question — split RTO/RPO commitments for multi-region failover

Carlos — thanks for the clear ask and the timing heads-up.

We can support differentiated RTO/RPO profiles between traffic classes, but it requires an operational carveout that we need to approve with product/infra and legal: specifically, pinning a hot standby in the EU for retail traffic while accepting longer recovery for analytics. That has two immediate impacts:

1) Cost/Capacity: reserving hot standby capacity in-region increases committed GPU capacity and monthly fees. I can get a quantified uplift from capacity planning.
2) Operational fallthrough: we need an agreed mutual action plan (MAP) for the switchover window — who initiates, who validates health, and automated fallback thresholds.

Next steps i propose:
- I’ll loop in Marissa (sales lead) and Naomi (legal) to surface contract carve points.
- Can you share the runbook excerpt and network diagram (you mentioned) by EOD? That will let infra size the standby and give a firm cost delta.
- If procurement needs a draft addendum before Wednesday, we can fast-track a conditional carveout that includes: prioritized hot-standby for retail, documented MAP, a 90-day post-go-live review.

I’ll also prep a short options matrix (capacity delta / expected monthly uplift / SLA language) and shoot it back to you by Monday.

—Karthik
Director, Solutions (Redwood Inference)

Attachment: none

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA question — split RTO/RPO commitments for multi-region failover

Karthik / team — looping infra and finance to get numbers. Quoting Carlos below for context.

> EU retail traffic: RTO = 00:30, RPO = 00:10
> Non-critical analytics (EU): RTO = 02:00, RPO = 01:00

Engineering notes from my quick sync with Ben (cc):
- To reliably guarantee 30m RTO for retail we need pinned hot-standby in eu-west with pre-warmed model instances for the retail-serving model family. This increases committed vGPU hours by ~22–30% depending on concurrency distribution.
- For analytics traffic we can rely on warm standby with faster cache-warm strategies; less capacity reserve required.

Legal (Naomi):
- We can draft an SLA addendum that enumerates traffic classes and the MAP, but we should include explicit failure modes where the carveout will not apply (e.g., region-wide cloud provider outage that triggers global capacity shortages).

Financial/ops ask: can we offer a conditional 90-day trial with a roll-back to standard SLOs if operational cost or test failure exceeds thresholds? If Nectar agrees, we can provide precise uplift numbers and a draft addendum to share with their procurement.

Ben — can you run a quick capacity estimate and send a delta by EOD PST? Naomi — can you take a first pass on the carve language and exclusions? I’ll coordinate with Carlos on the MAP and timeline.

—Marissa
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: capacity_delta_request.xlsx (placeholder)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@nectarfin.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Mar 2028 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA question — split RTO/RPO commitments for multi-region failover

Carlos — thanks for the patience. Summary and proposal below (see attached SLA_draft_redline_v3.pdf and network diagram):

Proposal (conditional carveout / trial):
- Priority mapping:
  * Retail (EU): guaranteed RTO 00:30, RPO 00:10 — requires pinned hot standby in eu-west and pre-warmed model instances for retail-serving models.
  * Analytics (EU): RTO 02:00, RPO 01:00 — warm standby with accelerated cache-warm strategy.
- Trial: 90-day conditional trial beginning on go-live; post-trial review to assess operational costs and availability metrics. If trial fails defined thresholds (see SLA addendum section 2.3) Redwood may revert to standard regional SLOs with 30 days' notice.
- MAP: Mutual action plan included; runbook ownership, switchover initiator (Nectar ops), health validation steps, and rollback criteria documented.
- Exclusions: global cloud provider outage, force majeure, or sustained resource exhaustion across all regions — carveout will not apply.

Cost delta (preliminary): pinned hot-standby increases committed monthly spend by ~27% for retail-serving model fleet. Ben will provide exact numbers within 24 hours.

Next steps:
1) Carlos — confirm Nectar's acceptance of the conditional-trial framing and that your procurement can present the addendum to legal on Wednesday.
2) Carlos — please send the runbook excerpt and network diagram if you haven’t already.
3) Naomi/Marissa/Ben — finalize contract language, capacity delta, and a one-page summary for procurement.

If acceptable, we’ll prepare the DocuSign package and target signature prior to your kickoff.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-minute call if you want to run the MAP live.

—Karthik
Director, Solutions (Redwood Inference)

Attachments: SLA_draft_redline_v3.pdf; multi_region_network_diagram.png
